pr_title: perf: optimize imports that are not mutated or reassigned
pr_body:
closes https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/8933

This is especially useful for generating smaller code when using [Vite's asset imports](https://vitejs.dev/guide/assets.html). This is not especially useful yet if using an `Image.svelte` component as that still won't be optimized, but if using the import directly or via a proposed preprocessor (https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/pull/9787#issuecomment-1572876158) it will greatly reduce the size of the generated code
pr_comments: I vaguely remember that @tanhauhau tried something similar in the context of not rerunning `$:` at one point, but it resulted in false negatives (i.e., `$:` wasn't rerunning as expected anymore). I'm not sure if this is related or different since it only applies to primitive constant values.

Hmm. I couldn't really find anything like that in his PR history - though maybe I missed it. Could https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/5045 possibly be what you were thinking of? The only other things I saw that were semi-related were PRs for the `@const` tag, https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/7426, and https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/6525.
What's an example snippet which shows how the code is smaller now?

issue_context.title: Consider imports that are not updated or mutated to be constant
issue_context.body:
### Describe the problem This gets converted to 50 lines of JS: ``` ``` And it scales really well. If you put 5 pictures inside a `
` you end up with 50 lines of JS. I believe the concise output here is courtesy of https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/7426 in Svelte 4.0. On the other hand, this gets converted to 112 lines of JS: ``` ``` And it doesn't scale nearly as nicely. If you put just 2 pictures inside a `
` you end up with 176 lines of JS. But if we want to use things like Vite's [asset handling](https://vitejs.dev/guide/assets.html), we have to write code that looks a lot more like the second. This ends up being important if we implement the Svelte image tag as a preprocessor as @Rich-Harris has proposed (https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/pull/9787#issuecomment-1572876158). The preprocessor approach doesn't scale as well as an `Image` component at the moment, but I believe it'd do even better if we made this change. ### Describe the proposed solution I'm hoping it'd be easy at least with the constant primitives. With the constant object you might have to do a bit more work to see that nothing's touching it. If it helps analyze it, we could create those objects wrapped in `Object.freeze` or something to indicate that they're not modified. ### Alternatives considered Don't get that final point on Lighthouse :laughing: ![Screenshot from 2023-07-06 20-16-20](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/assets/322311/bc07dc3a-c554-451a-9cad-4f14ac0e4e63) ### Importance nice to have
comments: Hmm. Thinking about this a bit more... In the case of handling images it's not actually `const` that we have, but a default `import`. I guess with an `import` the Svelte compiler doesn't resolve it and doesn't know if it's an immutable primitive or mutable object or whatnot. It might be hard to handle in the general case, but I think there's a lot we could do to make things easier since we're writing these asset imports and know they're immutable. E.g. similar to `/*#__PURE__*/` comment, perhaps we could write the preprocessor to output a new `/*#__IMMUTABLE__*/` comment telling Svelte that it's safe to assume it's immutable and optimize it.

I realized we wouldn't have to create a new comment like `/*#__IMMUTABLE__*/` because we already have `/** @readonly */` in JSDoc: https://jsdoc.app/tags-readonly.html And probably we wouldn't actually inline the constants , but just do string interpolation. I.e. convert it to: ``` ` ` ```

I'm thinking a good way to implement this actually would be to have a new compiler option that accepts a regex for determining whether an import is an asset and thus immutable. Then `vite-plugin-svelte` could provide Vite's [`DEFAULT_ASSETS_RE`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/71ceb0421afdedcaddd98712b9b7b6bfbf2af590/packages/vite/src/node/constants.ts#L133) to the Svelte compiler.
